Rashi on Eruvin 13b:11:2.hebrew: ושונין דבריהן ודברי בית שמאי - כשהיו ב"ש מביאין ראיה לדבריהם מן התורה, וב"ה מביאין ראיה ממקרא אחר, והיו ב"ה דורשין את המקרא של ב"ש למה בא, ולא היה קל בעיניהם — כאותה ששנינו במסכת ברכות (ד' י:): ב"ש אומרים: בערב כל אדם יטה ויקרא, ובבקר יעמוד, שנאמר: "בשכבך ובקומך". וב"ה אומרים: כל אדם קורא כדרכו, שנאמר: "ובלכתך בדרך". אם כן, למה נאמר "בשכבך ובקומך"? בשעה שדרך בני אדם שוכבין, ובשעה שדרך בני אדם עומדין:
Rashi on Eruvin 13b:11:2.english: And they would teach their statements and the statements of Beit Shammai - When Beit Shammai would bring a proof for their statements from the Torah, and Beit Hillel would bring a proof from another verse, Beit Hillel would expound Beit Shammai's verse [to explain] why it came [into Scripture], and it was not of slight consequence in their eyes — like that which we learned in tractate Berakhot (10b): Beit Shammai say: In the evening, every person should recline and recite [the Shema], and in the morning he should stand, as it is stated: "When you lie down and when you rise up" (Deuteronomy 6:7). And Beit Hillel say: Every person recites in his [usual] manner, as it is stated: "And when you walk by the way" (ibid.). If so, why is it stated: "When you lie down and when you rise up"? At the time when people usually lie down, and at the time when people usually rise.

Rashi on Eruvin 13b:11:3.hebrew: שמקדימין דברי ב"ש לדבריהן - דקאמרי להו: מעשה שהלכו זקני ב"ש, והדר זקני ב"ה:
Rashi on Eruvin 13b:11:3.english: That they prioritize the statements of Beit Shammai over their own statements - For they said to them: "An incident occurred in which the Elders of Beit Shammai went," and then, "the Elders of Beit Hillel."

Rashi on Eruvin 13b:13:1.hebrew: הדוחק את השעה - מתיגע להעשיר ולהתגדל, ורואה שאינו מצליח, ואעפ"כ חוזר והולך למרחקים, ומכניס עצמו לגבוהות:
Rashi on Eruvin 13b:13:1.english: One who forces the moment - [He] toils to become wealthy and to attain greatness, and sees that he is not succeeding, and nevertheless repeatedly travels to distant places and thrusts himself into lofty matters.

Rashi on Eruvin 13b:13:2.english: The hour stands for him - After some time, a successful hour is destined to stand for him.

Rashi on Eruvin 13b:14:1.hebrew: יפשפש מעשיו - שעשה כבר, ויבדוק עבירות שבידו, ויתודה וישוב:
Rashi on Eruvin 13b:14:1.english: He should examine his actions - [Those] that he has already done; and he should inspect the transgressions in his hand, and confess and repent.

Rashi on Eruvin 13b:14:2.hebrew: ימשמש במעשיו - כגון: אם בא מצוה לידו, יחשב הפסד מצוה כנגד שכרה, ולא יניח לעשותה בשביל ההפסד, שהרי שכרה עתיד לבוא. ואם באת לידו עבירה, יחשב שכרו שמשתכר בה עכשיו כנגד הפסדה העתיד ליפרע ממנו:
Rashi on Eruvin 13b:14:2.english: He should scrutinize his actions - For example: If a mitzvah comes to his hand, he should calculate the loss [incurred by] the mitzvah against its reward, and he should not refrain from performing it on account of the loss, for behold, its reward is destined to come. And if a sin comes to his hand, he should calculate the reward that he earns from it now against its loss that is destined to be exacted from him.

Rashi on Eruvin 13b:15:1.english: Wide enough to hold a half-brick - So that it will resemble a permanent structure, [fit] to build a building upon it.

Rashi on Eruvin 13b:15:2.english: And a half-brick [is] half a brick of three handbreadths - Thus, a half-brick is a handbreadth and a half in width.

Rashi on Eruvin 13b:15:3.hebrew: דייה לקורה ברוחב טפח כדי לקבל אריח זה ברחבו - ובגמרא פריך: טפח ומחצה בעי:
Rashi on Eruvin 13b:15:3.english: It is sufficient for the beam [to be] a handbreadth in width in order to hold this small brick across its width - And in the Gemara, it asks: A handbreadth and a half is required!

Rashi on Eruvin 13b:16:1.english: [If] it was of straw, etc. - Rabbi Yehuda says this.

Rashi on Eruvin 13b:17:1.english: [If it is] curved - Such that a half-brick cannot rest upon it.

Rashi on Eruvin 13b:17:2.hebrew: עגולה - ואין אריח יכול לעמוד עליה, אבל עבה היא, שאם תחלק, יהא רחבה טפח:
Rashi on Eruvin 13b:17:2.english: [If it is] round - And a half-brick cannot rest upon it, but it is thick [enough] that if it were split, its width would be a handbreadth.

Rashi on Eruvin 13b:17:3.hebrew: רואין אותה כאלו היא מרובעת - נפסלת או חלוקה. ואי זו היא מדת עגולה להכשיר:
Rashi on Eruvin 13b:17:3.english: One considers it as though it were square - [As if it were] hewn [square] or split. And what is the measure of a round [beam] to render [it] fit?

Rashi on Eruvin 13b:17:4.hebrew: כל שיש בהקיפה ג' טפחים - שצריכה חוט ארוך ג' טפחים להקיפה סביב, בידוע שיש בה רוחב טפח אם תחלק:
Rashi on Eruvin 13b:17:4.english: Any [beam] that has three handbreadths in its circumference - That requires a cord three handbreadths long to encircle it around — it is known that it has a width of a handbreadth if it is split.

Rashi on Eruvin 13b:1:1.english: And reconsidered - And changed his mind about divorcing her.

Rashi on Eruvin 13b:1:2.hebrew: פסול - אלמא וכתב לה משמע לשמה, הכי נמי כתיב ועשה לה — משמע לשמה:
Rashi on Eruvin 13b:1:2.english: [It is] invalid - Evidently, "and he shall write for her" means for her sake; so too, it is written: "and he shall perform with her" — which means for her sake.

Rashi on Eruvin 13b:2:1.english: There, it is written: “For her” - With regard to writing.

Rashi on Eruvin 13b:2:2.hebrew: הכא - כתיב לה לגבי עשייה. עשייה היינו מחיקה:
Rashi on Eruvin 13b:2:2.english: Here - It is written "for her" with regard to performance. Performance means erasure.

Rashi on Eruvin 13b:3:1.hebrew: על סוף דעתו - לא יכלו להבין באיזה דבריו נכונים, ובאיזה אין דבריו נכונים, שהיה נותן דעת מיושב והגון על אין הלכה כהלכה:
Rashi on Eruvin 13b:3:1.english: To the depth of his mind - They were unable to understand in which [cases] his statements were correct, and in which his statements were not correct, for he would provide a sound and cogent rationale for that which is not the halakhah as [though it were] the halakhah.

Rashi on Eruvin 13b:5:1.hebrew: דחזיתיה לרבי מאיר מאחוריה - כשלמדתי לפניו, ישבתי בשורה של אחריו:
Rashi on Eruvin 13b:5:1.english: That I saw Rabbi Meir from behind - When I studied before him, I sat in the row behind him.

Rashi on Eruvin 13b:8:1.hebrew: נחש שממית - אדם ובהמה, ומביא טומאה בעולם:
Rashi on Eruvin 13b:8:1.english: A snake that kills - People and animals, and brings impurity into the world.

Rashi on Eruvin 13b:8:2.hebrew: טהור - כשמת, דהא שמונה שרצים כתיבי:
Rashi on Eruvin 13b:8:2.english: [Is] ritually pure - When it dies, for [only] eight creeping animals are written [in the Torah].

Rashi on Eruvin 13b:9:1.hebrew: הכי גרסינן - מעשה קוץ בעלמא קעביד:
Rashi on Eruvin 13b:9:1.english: This is the version we read - "It merely performs the action of a thorn."

Tosafot on Eruvin 13b:14:1.hebrew: נוח לו לאדם שלא נברא - והא דאמרינן בפ"ק דע"ג (ד' ה.): "בואו ונחזיק טובה לאבותינו, שאילמלי הן לא חטאו, לא באנו לעולם" — הא מפרש התם: אימא, "כמי שלא באנו לעולם". א"נ: הכא איירי בסתם בני אדם, אבל צדיק — אשריו ואשרי דורו:
Tosafot on Eruvin 13b:14:1.english: It is preferable for man not to have been created - And that which we say in the first chapter of Avodah Zarah (5a): "Come and let us be grateful to our ancestors, for had they not sinned, we would not have come into the world" — behold, [the Gemara] explains there: Say, "[It would have been] as though we had not come into the world." Alternatively, here [the Gemara] is dealing with ordinary people, but [as for] a righteous person — fortunate is he and fortunate is his generation.

Tosafot on Eruvin 13b:2:1.hebrew: עשייה דידה מחיקה היא - ואם תאמר: אם כן, למה אין מוחקין לה מן התורה? ואומר ר"י: משום דכתיב "וכתב את האלות האלה", דבעינן שתהא כתיבה לשם אלה:
Tosafot on Eruvin 13b:2:1.english: "The action in her case is erasure" - And if you say: If so, why may one not erase [the passage] for her from a Torah scroll? And the Ri says: Because it is written: "And [the priest] shall write these curses" (Numbers 5:23), for we require that the writing be for the sake of the curse.

Tosafot on Eruvin 13b:7:1.hebrew: שיודע לטהר את השרץ - תימה: מאי חריפות הוא לטהר את השרץ, שהתורה טמאתו בהדיא? ואומר רבינו תם, דלענין טומאת נבילות איירי, שלא יטמא כזית ממנו במשא; דהא כתיב: "או בנבלת חיה", ושרץ, אע"פ שרוחש, הוי בכלל חיה, כמו נחש — דדרשינן בסנהדרין בפרק ארבע מיתות (סנהדרין ד' נט:): "ובכל חיה הרומשת" — זה נחש. ויליף רבינא ק"ו מנחש, דיצא מכלל נבלת חיה, דממעט ליה בתורת כהנים מטומאת נבילות מ"וכל הולך על גחון". וכי מסיק: "ולא היא", וסותר הקל וחומר — מ"מ אתי במה מצינו שפיר מנחש: דלא הוי בכלל חיה, ה"נ כל שרצים שרוחשין לא הוו בכלל חיה. ולא מצא ר"י בתורת כהנים שממעט בשום מקום נחש מטומאת נבילות. ועוד קשיא לר"י, דבהדיא ממעט בת"כ כל שרצים מטומאת נבילות, דקתני התם: היא מטמאה במשא, ואין שרצים מטמאים במשא. שיכול: ומה בהמה, שלא עשה הכתוב דמה כבשרה, מטמאה במשא — שרץ, שעשה דמו כבשרו, אינו דין שיטמא במשא? ת"ל: "היא" — ולא שרץ. ומיהו י"ל: אע"ג דאיכא מיעוטה, עביד נמי ק"ו; אבל קשיא: היכי אתי רבינא לבטל הק"ו שבתורת כהנים? ואי לאו דאיכא מיעוטא בהדיא, אדרבה, הוה עבדינן ק"ו דתורת כהנים! ועוד, דעל ק"ו דרבינא איכא למיפרך: מה לנחש, שכן טהור אפילו במגע בכעדשה:
Tosafot on Eruvin 13b:7:1.english: "Who knew how to purify the creeping animal" - It is astonishing: What sharpness is there in declaring pure the creeping animal, which the Torah explicitly deemed impure?! And Rabbeinu Tam says that it refers to the impurity of carcasses [tum'at neveilot], [namely,] that an olive's bulk [k'zayit] of it should not transmit impurity through carrying [massa]. For behold, it is written: "Or in the carcass of an [impure] beast" (Leviticus 5:2); and a creeping animal, even though it crawls, is included in [the general category of] "beast" [chayah], like a snake — as we expound in Sanhedrin in chapter Arba Mitot (Sanhedrin 59b): "'And over every beast that creeps' [Genesis 1:28] — this is the snake." And Ravina derived an a fortiori argument [kal va-chomer] from a snake, which was excluded from the general category of "the carcass of a beast," as it is excluded in Torat Kohanim from the impurity of carcasses from [the verse] "Whatever goes on its belly" (Leviticus 11:42). And when [the Gemara] concludes: "And it is not so," and refutes the a fortiori argument, nonetheless it is properly derived via an analogy [mah matzinu]: Just as a snake is not included in [the category of] "beast," so too all creeping animals that crawl are not included in [the category of] "beast." However, the Ri did not find anywhere in Torat Kohanim that it excludes a snake from the impurity of carcasses. And furthermore, it was difficult for the Ri: for in Torat Kohanim it explicitly excludes all creeping animals from the impurity of carcasses, as it is taught there: "[A beast] imparts impurity through carrying, but creeping animals do not impart impurity through carrying. For [one might] have thought: If a domesticated animal [behemah], whose blood Scripture did not treat like its flesh, imparts impurity through carrying, is it not logical that a creeping animal, whose blood Scripture treated like its flesh, should impart impurity through carrying? Scripture therefore states: 'It' — and not a creeping animal." And however, one could say: Even though there is an exclusion [in the verse], one may also construct an a fortiori argument; but it is difficult: How could Ravina come to overturn the a fortiori argument that is in Torat Kohanim? For had there not been an explicit exclusion, on the contrary, we would have applied the a fortiori argument of Torat Kohanim [which would render it impure through carrying]! And furthermore, against Ravina's a fortiori argument one can refute: What [can be derived from] a snake, seeing that it is pure even through contact in [the measure of] a lentil's bulk?!
